big/big: The Nix package collection is one enormous expression, with a huge number of packages defined inside it.
big/ask: You ask it for one package, and it answers in moments. To see how, we need one more piece of the language.
big/let: The word let gives names to values, and those names exist only in the expression after the word in.
big/order: The bindings can use each other, in any order. Here b uses a, and a is written after it.
big/value: These are not steps to run from the top. They are definitions. And the result is three.
lazy/throw: The function throw stops evaluation with an error. At least, it does when it runs.
lazy/let: Here x is a throw, and the whole expression is still one. Nothing asked for x, so Nix never worked it out.
lazy/thunk: A binding holds a promise of its value: how to compute it, if anyone ever needs it. That promise is called a thunk.
lazy/set: Sets work the same way. One value here is a throw, and selecting the other is fine.
lazy/bang: Select the throw itself, and that is when it goes off.
lazy/names: built-ins dot attr names reads only the names, so the values stay untouched.
lazy/len: And a list knows its length without computing what is in it.
self/how: Values wait, so a binding can mention a name whose value is not worked out yet. It can even mention the set it is in.
self/ok: Here z reads x dot y out of its own set. That works: computing z needs only y, and y is there.
self/rec: Reck, from before, relies on the same thing. The value of a waits until something asks, and then b is there.
self/bad: The trouble starts only when a value truly needs itself. To get x, Nix has to get x first.
self/err: There is no way out of that, and Nix stops with infinite recursion.
pkgs/mini: Here is the package collection in miniature: one big set, where each package is a value that can name the others.
pkgs/ask: Ask for curl, and Nix works out curl. Curl needs zlib, so zlib is worked out too.
pkgs/broken: The broken package sits in the same set, and it does no harm. Nobody asked for it.
pkgs/scale: Scale that up. The collection can define every package it has, and Nix computes only the ones you ask for, and what those need.
